built_pages_note: Measured 2026-09-06 (paper lap 11) by paper/measure_pages.py: 23 pages under Carlito, page objects and page-tree /Count agreeing, gated by check_paper.py against the author's 25-page rule (NH-028). Two pages of margin. It was 22 at lap 10; the page went to 90 words in SS4.4 and SS4.5 - one mandatory correction (the repository narrowed its own buffer-width claim, so the manuscript's 'two documents' became one), one clause, and the lap reviewer's block, which cost SS4.4 a sentence and SS4.5 an attribution. Measured before the reviewer's fixes: the mandatory correction ALONE (8,746 words) already rendered 23, so SS4.5 sat on a page boundary and any edit to it tipped the same page. That is why the words-to-pages table in paper/README.md is a 500-word sampling and not a rate. F9_present_perimeter is still drawn, committed and NOT referenced by the manuscript (paper/GAPS.md, gap G8, NH-032 open), so it still costs no page here and will cost one when it is referenced. THE FACE IS PART OF THE NUMBER: metric-compatible Carlito stands in for the non-redistributable Calibri build_docx.py asks for, so the gate reports and falls back to the 9,000-word proxy on any face whose metrics are not Calibri's. built_pages_inputs is the WFG-116 anchor: the digest of the document this 23 was measured on (the ordered figure list with pixel sizes, the table and reference counts, the body-word count). It does NOT re-derive the page count and nothing in this file does. Set both fields to null rather than hand-writing an anchor no run produced. WFG-116's other half, an apt line in auto-gates.yml so a clean clone measures, is open and outside paper/.
